label: General — any role
sub: Built for a full-time search: mornings on the skills and work samples your role needs, afternoons on applications, outreach, and interview practice.
weighting: This track covers what almost every loop asks for, whatever the role: a clear story, proof of your top skills, tailored applications, and practice on the exercise your field uses — case, presentation, portfolio review, role-play, or take-home. If your field has a specific round, spend the 9:00 block on it. Switch tracks above for algorithms and system design.
rules: Put a timer on every practice block. Record yourself answering interview questions and listen back once for rambling and missing results. Keep a notebook of what was hard and what you changed — the fix is what transfers, not the question.

resources.d: Free practice questions for any role, with feedback on your answers
Resumes, cover letters, negotiation, and awkward situations, answered plainly
Interview questions and salary reports by company
Comp by company and level, tech and beyond
Salary ranges by title and city for roles levels.fyi does not cover
Situation, Task, Action, Result — every story ends with a number

schedule.h: Open this page. Clear the follow-ups due, pick today's three target roles, choose what you will practice.
Two hours on the exercise your loop uses: cases, portfolio pieces, decks, writing, mock calls. Timer on, then 15 minutes of notes on what to fix.
Three to five applications, each tailored: swap 2–3 resume bullets to match the posting. Log every one here before moving on.
Five messages: referrals, recruiters, alumni. Send every follow-up that is due today.
Note what was hard, write tomorrow's three targets, prep anything due tomorrow. Then stop — rest is part of the plan.

1.h: Ten minutes per target company: what they sell, recent news, why you. Then tailor two applications with what you found.

2.h: STAR stories on a timer, recorded. Listen back for rambling and missing results. Then rehearse the project deep-dive.

3.h: Ten minutes per target company: what they sell, recent news, why you. Then tailor two applications with what you found.

4.h: STAR stories on a timer, recorded. Listen back for rambling and missing results. Then rehearse the project deep-dive.

5.h: Book a mock (behavioral and your role's exercise on alternate weeks). At 4:00, retro: applications sent, response rate by source, what changes next week.

0.h: Set up Monday before bed: the week's target companies and what you will practice. Nothing else.

6.h: One application, one mock if it's scheduled, then rest.

"Tell me about yourself" in 90 seconds; the "why are you looking" answer; what you're looking for
Record yourself answering the six most common questions for your role

15 applications logged, each with 2–3 resume bullets tailored to the posting

focus: Your most complex project: what you owned, the numbers, what you would change

items.t: Prepare a 5-minute deep-dive on your best project with numbers; practice "why that choice?" three levels deep

focus: Tailor your top 5 stories to each company with active interviews — their values, their language

focus: Take-homes and presentations: scope tight, show your thinking, finish early
